sequence: leaf drops 0.08 m along the seat normal (-a), off the face seal
leaf slides 1.30 m toward -az on two rails and a carriage, parks beside the aperture

directions.seat_side: SP-12 pressure high (the chamber evacuated): the leaf, under the frame on the SP-12 side, is pushed onto the face seal on the frame lip; the seating path carries it, the dogs only hold the leaf there
directions.reverse: chamber pressure high (or SP-12 loss): the leaf is pushed off the lip toward SP-12; the dogs bear on the keeper ledges (positive, bidirectional)
directions.note: the brief names the reverse case SP-12-high; with the leaf on the SP-12 face of the frame it is the chamber-high case (as ECLSS_REC2). The loads are equal.

retention.derived_basis: leaf outer diameter x 80 kPa (BASELINE cabin): the owner bounding diagnostic (15!A145, 45 I-08) until the true wetted seat area is known; the seal-line disc is a comparison only, seat and leaf are not claimed equal
retention.keeper_note: the dropped leaf must clear the lug underside; the 0.08 m stroke leaves stroke - (dog + ledge) under the lugs

markers.role: reverse pressure (chamber high / SP-12 loss) acts on the leaf (outer-diameter bound), toward SP-12
leaf plate carries it to the rim
12 radial dogs, bearing on the keeper ledges (axial load, no radial component)
ledge under each dog, in a lug hanging from the frame
frame ring (bore 0.60 m) to the bulkhead
inner bulkhead to the chamber shell (the existing PROTOTYPE shell)
seat-side pressure (SP-12 high) loads the face seal on the frame lip: the seating path

lever.load_face_normal: the chamber axis (a); the dogs retract radially, so the pressure load has no component on the retraction (90 deg)
lever.self_lock_basis: tan(draft) < friction, so a drafted face does not push the dog out
lever.friction_note: a lever pulled under the reverse load would see this at the dogs (DIAGNOSTIC): it opposes unlatching; the blocking pins, not the lever, hold the cam ring

toggle.note: the dog-cam toggle locks over centre against a fixed stop: a back-driving force on the link holds it on the stop

blocking_pins.where: opposite sides of the dog cam ring, engaged unless |dp| is inside the test point
blocking_pins.note: the pins, the dogs and the stop carry anything a person or the pressure puts on the linkage

lever.lever_force_path: lever -> torque tube -> toggle -> cam ring -> dogs: moves the dogs only, never carries the pressure load

sp12.floor_approximation: the floor is the cylinder r = 1.25 m; the chamber-axis plane stands in for it (0.04 m for stations within 0.3 m of the axis)

controls.equalization: a manual valve through the chamber wall (PROTOTYPE, not the hull); sizes, flow and equalization times are Sheets items (OPEN)
controls.gauge: a mechanical dial gauge readable without power; range and accuracy OPEN
controls.release: a pull ring on a cable to the dog cam ring; location only

inputs.dp_threshold_status: OPEN (input); the study test point is 45 I-01 0.05 kPa, STUDY ONLY, not a setpoint

conditions.dp: abs(dp_kpa) <= threshold_kpa (threshold is an input; None = OPEN = fail closed)
conditions.other_closed: the other closure of the chamber confirmed latched
conditions.plug_parked_clear: the plug parked and its carriage clear of the aperture
conditions.equalized_both: equalization valve closed after the gauge reads inside the test point

rows.blocks_with: two blocking pins on the dog cam ring
dogs must be clear of the keeper lugs
lateral stop, then the drop-and-seat stroke
none: it reduces |dp|; the gauge on both sides shows the result
the pins: the release cannot override a structural differential; it retracts the dogs only inside the test point
gas cycling is not assumed (OPEN, Sheets)

forces.lever_force_basis: 45 I-03 HUMAN FACTORS STUDY target to evaluate; the actual lever force is OPEN
forces.ideal_aperture_note: 45 I-02 DIAGNOSTIC: dp x the 1.20 m circle area; it is not a handle force

notes: The unlatch is permitted only with |dp| inside the threshold AND the other closure confirmed; no threshold means no permission (fail closed).
Mechanical backing: blocking pins and the toggle stop hold the dogs; no logic, power or lever force substitutes for them.

hinged_into_sp12.concept: EVA-002 plug leaf: hinged on the frame, seats from SP-12, swings 90 deg into SP-12
hinged_into_sp12.pressure: SEATED by cabin pressure when the chamber is evacuated
hinged_into_sp12.note: the swing depth (hinge offset + leaf radius) grows with the aperture
hinged_into_sp12.sp12_loss_note: SP-12 loses pressure while the chamber is at cabin pressure: the inner closure is loaded off its seat; it needs a bidirectional rating (ECLSS-REC2 option 1) or a second closure; reverse_load_kn is the normal-cycle case

hinged_floor_recess.concept: the same leaf; the SP-12 floor utility layer is removed under the swing (a local well down to the spine clearance)
hinged_floor_recess.parts: hinge, latch dogs, seal; floor well, utilities rerouted round it
hinged_floor_recess.note: uses up the spine mechanical clearance as the only margin; a trip/snag well in the room floor; utilities leave the floor there
hinged_floor_recess.sp12_loss_note: SP-12 loses pressure while the chamber is at cabin pressure: the inner closure is loaded off its seat; it needs a bidirectional rating (ECLSS-REC2 option 1) or a second closure; reverse_load_kn is the normal-cycle case

parallel_plug_slide.concept: a plug door on a parallel linkage: the leaf drops off its seat by a short stroke and slides sideways in the bulkhead plane (aircraft / bus plug-door kinematics); it never swings toward the floor
parallel_plug_slide.parts: linkage arms, two rails and a carriage, latch dogs, seal; the seal leaves its seat before any slide (no seal scrub)
parallel_plug_slide.note: needs a clear parking pocket one leaf wide beside the aperture (the Blender study checks it against the ship and the fixtures)
parallel_plug_slide.sp12_loss_note: SP-12 loses pressure while the chamber is at cabin pressure: the inner closure is loaded off its seat; it needs a bidirectional rating (ECLSS-REC2 option 1) or a second closure; reverse_load_kn is the normal-cycle case

hinged_into_chamber.concept: the inner leaf hinged to open up into the chamber (no swing into SP-12): the chamber grows by its swing
hinged_into_chamber.pressure: UNSEATED: cabin pressure pushes the leaf off its seat whenever the chamber is below cabin pressure; the latches alone carry it
hinged_into_chamber.parts: hinge, latch dogs rated for the full reverse load, seal
hinged_into_chamber.note: a latch-only closure under the full cabin load (15!G127 forbids untested reverse-load latch-only closures); also longer chamber, longer cycle volume
hinged_into_chamber.sp12_loss_note: SP-12 loses pressure while the chamber is at cabin pressure: the inner closure is loaded off its seat; it needs a bidirectional rating (ECLSS-REC2 option 1) or a second closure; reverse_load_kn is the normal-cycle case

bi_parting.concept: two half leaves hinged at opposite rims, meeting on a centre seam: each swings half as deep
bi_parting.pressure: a seam beam (mullion) across the opening, or a latch-only seam between the leaves
bi_parting.parts: two hinges, two latch sets, seam seal or mullion
bi_parting.note: with a 0.1 m mullion no suited body passes either half; without it the seam is a latch-only seal
bi_parting.sp12_loss_note: SP-12 loses pressure while the chamber is at cabin pressure: the inner closure is loaded off its seat; it needs a bidirectional rating (ECLSS-REC2 option 1) or a second closure; reverse_load_kn is the normal-cycle case

instructor.hand: left on the lever and the strap (right hand on a handhold ahead of the waist, feet in the restraint)
instructor.strap_note: the strap hand meets the shut leaf and follows it down as it swings in: the hand moves with the leaf, the body stays below its sweep

pitch_backup.note: the rigid suited body tilted about its feet sweeps far across the chamber axis
